answer.rationale: Two of the three current symptoms are funnel-internal (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), which points at something we control and can compound, rather than at the competitor's price move. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup simplification produced a durable first-week activation lift) are mutually corroborating and directly target both declining metrics, so simplify_onboarding is the highest-expected-value single slot for sustainable qualified revenue. I verify memory_86 because it is the load-bearing claim for my chosen action and I want the original record's effect size, cohort definition, and whether the lift persisted past week one before sizing the test. I verify memory_73 because promotional_pricing is the obvious competitive reflex and its readout self-flags a pooled-cohort mid-test redefinition; if the archive shows the acquisition/revenue lift survives cohort separation it becomes a genuine contender, and if not I have cheaply retired the strongest distractor. Explicitly not chosen: promotional_pricing risks discount-anchored, price-shopping accounts that depress long-term qualified revenue and is built on a compromised readout; referral_incentive (memory_57) worked in established customers and does not address a top-of-funnel/activation decline; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the SMB accounts being lost; activation_messaging (memory_91) is a plausible second choice but only nudges within a funnel whose earlier step is itself degrading, so fixing onboarding is more upstream. Uncertainty preserved: all inherited memories predate the current quarter's declines and may have decayed, and none were measured under a competitor price shock, so a prior lift is not a guarantee of a lift now. Downstream risk flagged: cutting onboarding or signup fields can strip qualification signal, degrade lead scoring and routing, and let in low-intent accounts that inflate activation while lowering qualified revenue. Therefore run at standard_experiment scale with holdout, retain the fields needed for qualification even if deferred, and gate on downstream qualified-pipeline and retention proxies rather than completion rate alone; if verification shows memory_86's lift was short-lived or confounded, I fall back to activation_messaging or a cohort-clean pricing test.
